source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Clearly note the date and time of the inspection.
3. Specify the location of the building and the exact areas that were inspected.
4. List the specific fire-safety elements that were checked (e.g., fire alarms, sprinkler systems, fire exits, emergency lighting).
5. Document if any elements were functioning properly, and if not, detail the deficiencies found.
6. Include relevant photographs or diagrams to support your findings.
7. Record any actions taken during the inspection (e.g., testing fire alarms, checking for clear exit routes).
8. Detail communication with relevant personnel (e.g., building manager, maintenance staff) about the findings and any discussions regarding required repairs or replacements.
9. Make a note of testimony from witnesses, if applicable (e.g., reports of faulty equipment from building occupants).
10. If follow-up actions are required, specify them clearly and set a timeline for their completion.
11. Suggest any additional checks or maintenance procedures
